fscrypt_v2: Per encrypted directory tree / inode policy; file and filename encryption
dmcrypt_luks2: Whole block mapping or volume
object_aead: Per object/chunk/envelope and manifest
decision: Use object AEAD as semantic enforcement; layer fscrypt/LUKS where operationally justified.

fscrypt_v2: Offline filesystem access without installed policy key
dmcrypt_luks2: Offline block-device or volume access without active volume key
object_aead: Unauthorized, wrong-domain, corrupt, substituted, or tampered cache object
decision: These boundaries are complementary, not interchangeable.

fscrypt_v2: Native for file contents and filenames within protected trees
dmcrypt_luks2: Native for mapped blocks while mapping is closed; common XTS mode
object_aead: Native for each encrypted payload
decision: Require object AEAD; prefer at least one lower storage layer for stolen-media defense.

fscrypt_v2: Absent for ordinary file-content modes
dmcrypt_luks2: Absent for ordinary XTS; possible with dm-integrity authenticated modes, selected stack marks experimental
object_aead: Native tag verification over ciphertext and AAD
decision: Only object AEAD supplies required object-semantic authentication in the minimum profile.

fscrypt_v2: Indirect key-domain separation only; no HaloKV principal fields
dmcrypt_luks2: Volume unlock identity only; no HaloKV principal fields
object_aead: Explicit canonical principal/scope fields in AAD and KDF context
decision: Bind authoritative principal IDs in AAD and authorization, not display names or mutable OS labels.

fscrypt_v2: May appear as unavailable names/content; not a HaloKV miss contract
dmcrypt_luks2: Mapping activation failure or garbage/I/O behavior depending mode
object_aead: AEAD FAIL normalized to MISS_RECOMPUTE
decision: One external miss class; precise reason only in access-controlled telemetry.

fscrypt_v2: Filesystem/application-dependent
dmcrypt_luks2: May produce I/O errors only with supporting integrity; otherwise corruption may pass upward
object_aead: Envelope parse bounds + tag + identifier + manifest checks; any failure is miss
decision: Fail closed before decompression/deserialization.

fscrypt_v2: None
dmcrypt_luks2: None by default
object_aead: Not supplied by AEAD alone; can bind epoch/generation but needs trusted freshness state
decision: Maintain trusted epoch floors and manifest generations where freshness is required.

fscrypt_v2: Does not protect after keys are installed against privileged live compromise
dmcrypt_luks2: Does not protect after mapping is active
object_aead: Keys/plaintext available to authorized process; does not defeat compromised process/kernel
decision: Out of cryptographic at-rest scope; use OS isolation, least privilege, attestation only as separate controls.

fscrypt_v2: Possible directory-key separation plus OS access controls
dmcrypt_luks2: Weak if tenants share one unlocked mapping
object_aead: Strongest native cryptographic tenant/project binding if keys and AAD are separated
decision: Object AEAD mandatory for shared multi-user cache.

fscrypt_v2: Possible separate directory policies but operationally coarse
dmcrypt_luks2: Separate volumes/mappings are coarse
object_aead: Per-rank derived key within epoch; rank ID in AAD
decision: Use rank-local AEAD key domain and rank-local nonce state.

fscrypt_v2: Kernel/filesystem mode-specific; application does not manage object nonce
dmcrypt_luks2: Sector-IV mode managed by mapping configuration
object_aead: Explicit 96-bit nonce allocation and per-key uniqueness; epoch rollover on uncertain state
decision: Persist monotonic allocation safely or use randomly generated nonces under strict limits; never reuse intentionally.

fscrypt_v2: Filesystem master keys installed through fscrypt key APIs/keyrings
dmcrypt_luks2: LUKS2 keyslots/tokens unwrap volume key; boot via crypttab or orchestrator
object_aead: KMS/HSM/wrapped epoch roots; rank keys delivered to least-privileged service memory
decision: No plaintext long-lived rank key on cache media; record authority and key owner.

fscrypt_v2: Mount may proceed while protected names remain inaccessible until key installation
dmcrypt_luks2: Mapping may block, fail, or be optional depending crypttab/orchestrator policy
object_aead: Cache starts cold/read-disabled until key authorization; compute path remains authoritative
decision: Boot must fail closed for cache serving but should degrade to recomputation rather than plaintext cache.

fscrypt_v2: Open/in-use files can retain per-file keys after master-key removal
dmcrypt_luks2: Mapping close can fail while busy; deferred close is not immediate
object_aead: Process-held keys and already decrypted buffers survive until drained/wiped/terminated
decision: Drain, close/unmap, revoke, verify absence, then destroy key references; document incomplete eviction.

fscrypt_v2: New policy/key usually means migration/rewrite or new tree
dmcrypt_luks2: Credential/keyslot rotation differs from payload reencryption; reencryption has recovery modes
object_aead: New epoch for writes; old epoch read-only during bounded transition; lazy recompute preferred
decision: Prefer epoch rollover and cache recomputation over bulk in-place transformation.

fscrypt_v2: Directory-tree policy key
dmcrypt_luks2: Entire volume key / all data on mapping
object_aead: Tenant/project/prefix/rank/epoch scope; per-object with independent DEKs if required
decision: Choose hierarchy granularity according to deletion and incident requirements.

fscrypt_v2: Filesystem crash behavior; no application authenticity/freshness semantics
dmcrypt_luks2: Filesystem plus mapping; dm-integrity journal and LUKS reencryption resilience matter
object_aead: Immutable object write + atomic manifest publish; nonce state and epoch recovery are explicit
decision: Treat uncertain nonce counters or partially published manifests as miss/new epoch.

fscrypt_v2: Backup needs keys/policies and may expose names/metadata depending tool
dmcrypt_luks2: Raw volume plus protected LUKS header/key dependencies; header backups are sensitive
object_aead: Coherent ciphertext, authenticated manifests, format version, wrapped epochs, policy metadata
decision: No cache backup by default; quarantine and validate any restore.

fscrypt_v2: Filesystem block/file dedup interactions are filesystem-specific and can leak equality
dmcrypt_luks2: Below-filesystem encryption usually disrupts physical ciphertext dedup and reveals allocation via discard
object_aead: Scoped keyed CID enables authorized logical dedup; randomized ciphertext itself is not the stable key
decision: Private dedup ≤ tenant/project sharing scope; public/system namespace separate.

fscrypt_v2: Potentially tree-scoped only if all master/derived copies become inaccessible; busy files complicate
dmcrypt_luks2: Volume-scoped if all volume-key unlock paths, headers, backups, escrow, and snapshots are eliminated
object_aead: Epoch- or object-scoped depending independent key wrapping; all copies and backups still matter
decision: State scope and evidence; never claim physical zeroization.

fscrypt_v2: Filesystem discard behavior separate from encryption
dmcrypt_luks2: Pass-through discard leaks allocation and does not prove erase
object_aead: Logical deletion/key destruction does not command media sanitization by itself
decision: Use NIST SP 800-88r2-aligned media-specific procedure with verification/validation.

fscrypt_v2: Moderate; policy inheritance/keyring/busy-file caveats
dmcrypt_luks2: Moderate; boot dependencies, mappings, header backup, reencryption
object_aead: Highest implementation responsibility; envelope, canonicalization, nonce state, key authority, telemetry
decision: Complexity is justified because semantic tenant/object binding cannot be delegated to lower layers.

fscrypt_v2: Optional/conditional defense-in-depth for per-tenant or service directory isolation
dmcrypt_luks2: Recommended host-volume baseline where operationally supported
object_aead: Required minimum multi-user persistent-cache control
decision: Profile: object AEAD + optional fscrypt v2 + LUKS2/dm-crypt at host-volume layer.
